name: Wren Holloway-Singh
description:
Wren goes into places people are not supposed to be able to go into. Without augmentation. The unaugmented part is important — every corponation surveillance grid is calibrated to read augmented presences first, and Wren has spent fourteen years learning to register as the kind of presence the grids do not flag. She moves like a person who has never had access to a workout program more sophisticated than walking and stairs, and looks like that person, and then she is in the room and the room does not know she is there.

No BCI. No subdermal mesh. No vision augmentation. Her tools are a pair of climbing gloves she has owned for nine years, a small set of corporate-grade lockpicks that look identical to corporate maintenance keys (because she had a corporate maintenance keymaker fabricate them), and the kind of full-body fitness that comes from doing the work every day for fourteen years and refusing all the shortcuts. The street's most consistent rumour about Wren is that she has been augmented in some classified program that hides the augmentation from standard scans. The rumour is incorrect. Wren is, by every metric the rumour proposes, exactly as augmented as a Tier 1 dock worker who has never been able to afford it.
heritage: Welsh-Punjabi. Father's family from Cardiff via the British climate-collapse waves of the 2160s. Mother's family from Amritsar via three generations of London-to-Manchester resettlement. Wren grew up between London and Manchester and emigrated to the GLMZ in her mid-twenties for reasons she has not shared with anyone Kyle has met. Speaks Welsh badly, Punjabi well, English in the accent the operator-class GLMZ corridor uses.
specialty: physical infiltration; document and object recovery from secured locations; the kind of contract where the brief specifies that the asset must not know it was acquired; non-violent extraction
method: casework over days or weeks before any contract. Maps the surveillance grids and the human patterns. Identifies the entry window. Enters during the window. Leaves before the window closes. Returns the asset to the contractor. Does not stay for the after-action review.
code: she does not work contracts that require her to harm a person directly. She works contracts where harm is downstream of the asset she recovers, which she has accepted as the cost of working at all. The acceptance does not feel good to her. She has been seeing Aleksei (above) for talk-therapy purposes for two years, and Aleksei has not, by Wren's own assessment, helped her stop accepting the cost. He has helped her see the cost clearly, which she considers a different and possibly more useful service.
signature_gear: climbing gloves (nine years); a kit of corporate-maintenance-grade lockpicks she rotates through three storage caches in the GLMZ corridor; a single concealable knife she has drawn twice and used once; a wardrobe of unbranded clothing that registers as Tier 1 or Tier 2 depending on what the contract calls for; the absence of augmentation, which is the actual asset
relationship_to_kyle: professional, occasional. They have worked together once. Wren got Kyle inside; Kyle handled the extraction. The contract closed clean. Wren prefers Kyle's company to most of the other heavy elements she has worked with because Kyle does not advertise his discipline and Wren has learned to be suspicious of operators who advertise theirs.
aesthetic: small, lean, mid-thirties, looks like an office worker who walks home every day. Brown hair she keeps short for practical reasons. Wears the same kind of clothes most days, which is part of the cover and part of the temperament and part of the cost calculation.
spin_off_hook: A contract requires Wren to infiltrate a corponation facility that has, in the eight months since her last reconnaissance, installed a new class of surveillance hardware she has not seen before. The hardware is not augmentation-keyed. It is *unaugmentation*-keyed. The corponation has built a sensor grid specifically calibrated to detect the absence of the network signatures it expects civilians to produce, and Wren — the operator who has built her career on producing exactly that absence — is now the operator the grid is best designed to detect. The story is what she does about it.
